standard_prerequisites.name: General Kneser hypergraph and its chromatic number
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a hypergraph H the general Kneser hypergraph is the hypergraph whose vertices are the edges of H and whose edges are the r-tuples of pairwise disjoint edges of H; the article's own definition is retained at source lines 124-126, together with the remark there that its chromatic number is the special case of the tau-matching chromatic number in which every frequency equals r-1.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof colours this hypergraph with the colour set A and applies the lower bound for its chromatic number at source lines 324-326.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equitable colorability defect and the cited lower bound
standard_prerequisites.statement: The r-th equitable colorability defect of H is the minimum number of vertices whose removal leaves a subhypergraph admitting a proper vertex colouring with r colours whose class sizes differ by at most one; the article states at source lines 275-279 that the chromatic number of the general Kneser hypergraph of H is at least the ceiling of that defect divided by r-1. This is a cited result of Abyazi Sani, Alishahi, Azarpendar and Jafari, not a claim of the counted theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the augmented hypergraph at source lines 324-326 to convert the number of colours into a bound on the defect.

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible colour frequencies and matching colourings
standard_prerequisites.statement: An r-colour-frequency mapping assigns to each colour an integer below r; an (A,tau)-matching colouring of H colours the edges by colours of A so that every nonempty monochromatic matching has size at most the frequency of its colour; H is tau-admissible when such a finite A exists, and the tau-matching chromatic number is the least size of such an A (source lines 115-121).
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two objects and both conclusions of the counted theorem.

core_obligations: Fix an arbitrary finite colour set A of C admitting an (A,tau)-matching colouring c of H, since the theorem is a statement about every such A.

Build the augmented hypergraph H~ by adding r-1-tau(a) fresh vertices carrying singleton edges for every a in A with tau(a) < r-1, and extend c to an edge colouring c~ of H~ that colours each of those singleton edges by its own a (source lines 314-316).

Prove that c~ is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph of H~: any r pairwise disjoint monochromatic edges of colour a contain at most r-1-tau(a) of the new singleton edges, so at least tau(a)+1 of them lie in H and would be tau(a)+1 pairwise disjoint H-edges of colour a, contradicting the defining property of c (source lines 317-321).

Apply the cited lower bound for the Kneser chromatic number to H~ to get (r-1)|A| >= ecd^r(H~), and prove ecd^r(H~) >= |V(H~)|-|V(H)|+ecd^r(H) by observing that an equitably r-colourable induced subhypergraph cannot contain a singleton edge, so all dummy vertices must be removed and at least ecd^r(H) further vertices of H (source lines 328-335).
Combine (r-1)|A| = sum of tau over A plus |V(H~)|-|V(H)| with the defect inequality to obtain the bound on the sum of the frequencies, hence the bound on chi_M(tau,H) (source lines 337-343).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the theorem to an arbitrary finite A admitting an (A,tau)-matching colouring.
Augment H by singleton-edged dummy vertices and extend the colouring.
Verify that the extension is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph of the augmented hypergraph.
Apply the cited Kneser lower bound to the augmented hypergraph.
Bound the equitable colorability defect of the augmented hypergraph from below.
Arithmetic conclusion for the sum of the frequencies and for chi_M(tau,H).

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem mainthmSaeed2 at source lines 301-309: for a tau-admissible hypergraph H and an r-colour-frequency mapping tau it must produce a finite colour set B with sum of tau over B at least ecd^r(H) and must bound chi_M(tau,H) by the minimum size of a finite A with sum of tau over A at least ecd^r(H). The proof (source lines 311-345) augments H by adding r-1-tau(a) singleton-edged dummy vertices for every a in A, extends the matching colouring to them (source lines 314-321) and must check that the extension is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph of the augmented hypergraph, where the point is that r monochromatic disjoint edges contain at most r-1-tau(a) of the new singleton edges. The remaining step is the defect inequality ecd^r(H~) >= |V(H~)|-|V(H)|+ecd^r(H) (source lines 328-335), which needs the observation that no equitably r-colourable induced subhypergraph can keep a singleton edge, so all dummy vertices and at least ecd^r(H) original ones have to be removed. Neither step is a routine verification, but the cohomological input is the cited equitable-defect bound for the Kneser chromatic number stated at source lines 275-279 and is not re-proved here, so the counted material is rated H2 rather than H3.

compared.difference: Same source, different proposition: the counted public unit is the sharpness Proposition at source lines 358-360 with its own proof at 361-404, which claims that the two lower bounds are attained by complete uniform hypergraphs. The present card counts Theorem mainthmSaeed2 (source lines 301-309) with its own complete proof at 311-345; in the public unit this theorem appears only as retained context (manifest context span 301-309) and its proof is not retained there, so this is a different statement, not a repackaging of the counted unit.

compared.difference: The sibling card counts Theorem mainthmSaeed, whose lower bound is |V(H)| - alt_r(H) with the alternation number; the present card counts Theorem mainthmSaeed2, whose lower bound is the equitable colorability defect ecd^r(H). The article separates them into two different sections, states at source lines 285-292 that the two quantities are not comparable (each of the three comparison signs can occur), and the two proofs must establish different facts about the augmented hypergraph: alt_r(H~) = alt_r(H) at source line 218 against ecd^r(H~) >= |V(H~)|-|V(H)|+ecd^r(H) at source lines 328-335.
